findings.suggestedAction: fuse ui-audit,ux-audit
verdictReasons: UPHELD: Core record facts check out. registry/nodes/basic/ui-audit.json and ux-audit.json both exist as basic generics with no prerequisites. Named skills match: garrytan/design-review has genericSkillRef ui-audit, garrytan/plan-design-review and garrytan/devex-review have genericSkillRef ux-audit, and leonxlnx/redesign-skill has genericSkillRef ui-audit (3★). nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max is 4★ with origin true and TM 227.51 grade A, so 'TM 228, 4A' is a fair rounding. No fusion node has both ui-audit and ux-audit as prerequisites. design-generation lists ui-audit alongside code-generation and vision-qa, and web-accessibility and founder-mode-orchestration use ux-audit alone, so the 'no existing fusion over them' claim holds. Two inaccuracies in the supporting text: (1) the target 'ui-ux-audit' is not a node (no registry/nodes/**/ui-ux-audit.json), so the suggested fusion is really ui-audit+ux-audit; (2) 'ui-ux-pro-max already spans both' is not a record fact, since its genericSkillRef is ux-audit only. Both are content judgments rather than record errors, so the finding stands with those corrections.

REFUTED: Evidence basis is not sufficient or deterministic. (1) The core basis is an asserted co-usage pattern ('routinely used together'), which is model judgment and is not recorded in any registry field. META §6.2 requires skills that 'can be orchestrated in a single high-level workflow', and the finding does not show such an orchestration. (2) The registry does not support 'ui-ux-pro-max already spans both': nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max.md carries genericSkillRef ux-audit only, not ui-audit. Its prepass computedTm is 227.51 (grade A), not 228. (3) Of the cited sources, garrytan/devex-review, garrytan/plan-design-review and nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max map to ux-audit, while leonxlnx/redesign-skill and garrytan/design-review map to ui-audit. So the sources do not cleanly demonstrate a composite of the two. (4) The finding itself states medium confidence. Fusion nodes are structure, not scoring evidence, so the proposal rests on a judgment, not a deterministic signal. Checked: registry/nodes/basic/ui-audit.json, registry/nodes/basic/ux-audit.json, registry/named/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max.md, registry/named/leonxlnx/redesign-skill.md, registry/named/garrytan/devex-review.md, registry/named/garrytan/plan-design-review.md, registry/named/garrytan/design-review.md, META.md §6.2. The 'no existing fusion over both' claim holds: design-generation fuses ui-audit only and web-accessibility fuses ux-audit only. That does not rescue the basis, so the finding is refuted on evidence strength.

UPHELD: META.md §6.2 expressly allows fusing distinct specialized capabilities that can be orchestrated in one workflow into a new fusion-type generic, and META §1.2 defines fusion as any non-basic node with at least one prerequisite. Generic-over-basic fusions already exist (registry/nodes/fusion/web-accessibility.json = browser-control + ux-audit), so the proposed ui-audit + ux-audit fusion has precedent. The action is additive: it demotes nothing, lowers no TM, and transfers no Origin. The Yggdrasil IV ratification does not restrict it, and Fusion Score is informational only (§2.1e). Caveats that do not refute the finding: §6.2's clause that composites are 'promoted to higher star tiers' is subordinate to TM as sole promotion authority (§2.1e), so the finding's no-S-grade-implied framing is correct. Re-parenting garrytan/design-review and plan-design-review from ui-audit/ux-audit to a new bucket does not change branch, since branch derives from suiteComponents and rank (§1.2). Current Origin of ui-audit (leonxlnx/redesign-skill) and ux-audit (nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max) is per-bucket and would not be removed by an additive fusion. The reference to garrytan/devex-review as a UX-audit member is a stretch of the META text but goes to fit, not to a rule violation. Its rationale is usage co-occurrence, which is not a META rule, so it is a judgment call, not a prohibited action.
